text:
Matthew Robertson played 72 games for the Rangers last season, scoring six goals and 18 points, and Evolving-Hockey rated him 88th of 215 defensemen with 500-plus minutes, mostly for his even-strength offense. This season he has had to wait. He drew back into the lineup only on Nov. 7 and has played three games since, all at about 12 minutes a night.

One of them was a homecoming. The Edmonton native played at Rogers Place on Nov. 9, and Forever Blueshirts wrote that he "impresses in long-awaited Edmonton homecoming."

Three games is far too small a sample to judge. He has no points and one shot, and the Rangers have held a narrow edge in expected goals with him on at five on five. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had his weak spot last season in exits, with only 24% keeping possession. Our season range is wide because his role is uncertain: watch whether his ice time climbs back toward last season's level.
headline: Robertson is back in the Rangers lineup
